headline: INOMIN MINES CUTS 420M AT 0.22% NICKEL AT LYNX — SUMITOMO-BACKED DISCOVERY OPENS SECOND TARGET 10KM FROM BEAVER
snippet: Inomin Mines (TSX-V: MINE) drilled 420 metres at 0.22% total nickel and 23.5% magnesium from 2.5 metres downhole at the Lynx block in central British Columbia — a second discovery area 10 km south of its Beaver deposit, funded by a $2.3 million Sumitomo Metal Mining Canada exploration program. Shares jumped 33% to a new 12-month high of 15¢ on the Tuesday announcement, with assays from five additional holes still pending.

headline: ALLIED GOLD'S $500M KURMUK MINE BEGINS OPERATIONS IN ETHIOPIA — 240,000 OZ/YR TARGET AS EXPLORATION CONFIRMS DISTRICT SCALE
snippet: Allied Gold (TSX: AAUC) completed commissioning at its Kurmuk mine in Ethiopia on October 6, marking the start of commercial-scale operations at the $500 million project targeting 240,000 oz/yr for 10 years. Concurrent exploration at the adjacent Dish Mountain zone returned an 80.09-metre intercept at 1.53 g/t gold at Kiftet, extending the 9 km Tsenge Trend as the priority mine-life extension target.

headline: PRINCE SILVER NEVADA: WIDEST INTERCEPTS EVER — 47M AT 68 G/T AG AND 37M AT 86 G/T AS 9,000M PROGRAM CONTINUES
snippet: Prince Silver Corp. (CSE: PRNC) reported its two widest silver drill intercepts to date at the Prince Silver Project in Nevada, with holes PRC-59 and PRC-60 returning 47.24 metres at 68.2 g/t Ag (119 g/t AgEq) and 36.58 metres at 86.3 g/t Ag (146 g/t AgEq) from near-surface depths. The results extend a 1.5–2 kilometre mineralized strike length as the company advances an upsized 9,000-metre program toward a 2027 maiden mineral resource estimate.

headline: NEWCORE GOLD ENCHI: 41M AT 1.16 G/T GOLD BELOW EXISTING PIT SHELLS — 1.5 MOZ GHANA RESOURCE GROWING BENEATH RESERVES
snippet: Newcore Gold (TSX-V: NCAU) intersected 41 metres at 1.16 g/t gold — including 13 metres at 2.54 g/t — below the pit shells constraining its 1.5 Moz indicated resource at the Enchi Gold Project in Ghana. Drilling confirms high-grade mineralisation extending beneath current reserve limits across the Sewum, Nyam, and Boin deposits, with 40,528 metres in 272 holes achieving a 98% mineralisation hit rate.

headline: ANALYSTS: GOLD FIELDS WILL NEED TO OFFER MORE — $27B NORTHERN STAR BID 'TOO LIGHT' AS SOUTH AFRICAN MINER PRESSES HOSTILE APPROACH
snippet: Gold Fields (NYSE: GFI) is pressing its unsolicited A$38.7 billion ($27 billion) cash-and-scrip bid for Northern Star Resources after the Australian miner's board unanimously rejected the A$27-per-share offer as 'opportunistic.' Analysts say the 22%-premium bid — structured 74% as Gold Fields scrip — is priced too conservatively for a deal that would create the world's second-largest gold miner, and that Gold Fields will need a materially higher figure to win over Northern Star shareholders.

headline: GENESIS-VAULT A$12.6B GOLD MERGER HEADS TO LATE-OCTOBER SHAREHOLDER VOTE — ACCC CLEARED, AUSTRALIA'S 3RD-LARGEST GOLD PRODUCER ON THE TABLE
snippet: Genesis Minerals (ASX: GMD) dispatched its scheme booklet to Vault Minerals (ASX: VAU) shareholders in early October, with a vote on the A$12.6 billion merger expected late October 2026. The ACCC cleared the transaction unconditionally; if approved, the combined group will target 600,000–700,000 oz of annual gold output from Western Australia's Leonora-Laverton district — the country's third-largest listed gold producer — with $2 billion in targeted synergies.

headline: E3 LITHIUM EYES BANK FINANCING FOR CANADA'S LARGEST LITHIUM PLAY — $36.5M FEDERAL FUNDING, FID BY 2027 FROM ALBERTA DLE PROJECT
snippet: E3 Lithium (TSX: ETL) is advancing toward a final investment decision by late 2027 for its Clearwater Project in Alberta, holding Canada's largest lithium resource at 1.29 million tonnes LHM equivalent. The company secured $36.5 million in non-repayable federal funding to complete its direct lithium extraction (DLE) demonstration facility and feasibility study, targeting 12,000 tpa of battery-grade lithium carbonate from 2029 at a project located 130 km south of Calgary.

headline: NICKEL SINKS TO 2026 LOW AT $16,322/T; COBALT BREAKS BELOW $40K FOR FIRST TIME IN A YEAR — BATTERY METALS DIVERGE FROM COPPER SURGE
snippet: LME nickel fell to its 2026 low of $16,322 per tonne for the first half of October as Indonesia's NPI output remained elevated, while cobalt dropped below $40,000 per tonne for the first time since October 2025 on weak battery supply chain demand. The dual-floor dynamic reinforces nickel and cobalt's status as the cycle's laggards versus copper, lithium, and gold — widening the commodity split that is reshaping junior developer valuations.
